items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Edwards, I didn't hear the fellas called Edwards. You never worked with him? No, I never worked with him.

ctx.x: Well there was one more trumpet player I had on my list to ask about, it's Edwards. Edwards, Edwards, remember wasn't there one Ralph? Willie Edwards? Is it Willie Edwards or something? Willie Edwards. It was a dead-barred clam, I don't think we got it mixed up. I think Punch talked about Willie Edwards. Yeah, Willie Edwards and stuff. Do you remember?

Edwards, I didn't hear the fellas called Edwards. You never worked with him? No, I never worked with him. It might be some of Punch's. Might have been some fella from uptown around Punch's way, you know, because Punch came, he's from the country, you know Punch. He's from Raceland. Yeah, from Raceland. That's where he come from out there. He came here practically lived uptown all, you know what happened, he came here.
You were speaking about Freddie Kepard earlier. What kind of a style? Was he any different to the other trumpet players? No, no.
